name: 21s

why: Trains the biceps, brachialis and brachioradialis through a neutral or reverse grip. Adds forearm and elbow flexor thickness that standard curls miss.

cues: Focus on feeling the target muscle
Control the negative — slow eccentric builds more muscle
Full range of motion unless mobility is limiting

name: 45 Degree Back Extension
description: A back extension on a 45 degree hyperextension bench, hinging at the hips and lifting your torso back to a straight line from head to heels.
form_cues: Pad just below the hip bones, heels locked in, hinge at the hips with a neutral spine, rise until the body is in a straight line, no arching past it
why: Trains the lower back, glutes and hamstrings together through a full hip hinge, with very little load on the spine. A plate held at the chest makes it easy to add weight over time.
reps: Strength: 6-10 reps (weighted) | Hypertrophy: 10-15 reps | Endurance: 15-25 reps | 3-4 sets
cues: Set the pad just below your hip bones so you can fold forward freely
Cross your arms over your chest, or hold a plate there to make it harder
Hinge at your hips and lower with a flat back
Squeeze your glutes to lift back up
Stop when your body makes a straight line, without leaning back past it
Move slowly, especially on the way down

name: 45 Degree DB Press
description: A dumbbell press on a bench set to 45 degrees, which shifts more of the work to the upper chest and the front of the shoulders.
form_cues: Bench at 45 degrees, shoulder blades back and down, dumbbells lowered to the upper chest, elbows about 45-60 degrees from the body, press up and slightly in
why: The steeper angle puts more of the load on the upper chest and front delts than a flat press. Dumbbells let each arm work on its own and move through a longer range than a barbell.
reps: Strength: 6-8 reps | Hypertrophy: 8-12 reps | Endurance: 15-20 reps | 3-4 sets
cues: Set the bench to 45 degrees and sit right back into it
Pull your shoulder blades back and down before you start
Lower the dumbbells to your upper chest, elbows about 45 to 60 degrees from your body
Press up and slightly in until the dumbbells nearly touch
Keep your feet planted and your lower back on the bench
Take 2 to 3 seconds to lower each rep

name: 90-90 Breathing
description: Lying on the back with hips and knees at 90 degrees supported on a bench or wall, performing slow diaphragmatic breaths to reset core and breathing mechanics.
why: A foundational breathing and core-reset drill widely used in physical therapy to restore proper diaphragmatic breathing and reduce excess spinal extension.
cues: Breathe slowly into the belly and ribs
Keep the lower back gently flattened against the floor

name: 90/90 Hip IR/ER
description: A seated hip mobility drill. Sit with both knees bent to about 90 degrees, one hip externally rotated in front and the other internally rotated to the side, then rotate both knees across to the opposite side and repeat slowly.
form_cues: Tall seated posture, both knees at about 90 degrees, hips rotating (not the lower back), slow controlled switches, hands behind for support if needed
why: Moves the hips through both internal and external rotation, which are needed for squatting, lunging and changing direction. It is a simple way to check and build hip rotation range.
cues: Sit tall and keep the chest up
Keep both feet on the floor and move the knees across with control
Use your hands behind you for support if you need it
Move slowly and stay inside a range that feels comfortable
Keep the movement at the hips, not the lower back

name: 90/90 Hip Stretch

Avoid shrugging or excessive arching through the spine

Front knee stays in line with toes
Drive through front heel to stand

Catch the dumbbells at the shoulders with soft knees
Keep the dumbbells close to the body throughout

name: Dumbbell Cossack Lunge

Sit back into the working hip, not just down

name: Dumbbell Cossack Squat

Push through the working heel to return to centre

Step diagonally behind, not straight back
Keep most of the weight on the front leg

name: Dumbbell Deadlift
description: Deadlift pattern performed holding a dumbbell in each hand, a beginner-friendly entry point into hip hinge loading.

Hinge at the hips, chest stays proud
Push the floor away to stand up

name: Dumbbell Fly

Think hugging a tree — arc motion, not press
Stretch at the bottom — feel the chest open

name: Dumbbell Forward Lunge
description: Forward lunge performed holding a dumbbell in each hand, adding resistance to the standard walking lunge pattern.
why: Adds progressive load to a foundational lunge pattern once the bodyweight version becomes too easy.

Push back through the front heel to return

name: Dumbbell Front Raise
description: Standing single or bilateral front raise isolating anterior deltoids
form_cues: Standing feet shoulder-width, raise to shoulder height, slight elbow bend
why: Targets the front deltoid through forward flexion of the shoulder. Develops anterior delt fullness and strength for pressing movements.

name: Dumbbell High Pull
description: Single or double dumbbell variation of the high pull, useful for teaching the pull pattern with less technical demand than a barbell.
why: Lower barrier to entry than barbell high pull while still building explosive pulling power and shoulder stability.

Elbows lead the movement, not the hands

name: Dumbbell Incline Press
description: A dumbbell press on an incline bench angled 30-45 degrees targeting the upper chest.
form_cues: Incline 30-45°, full ROM, dumbbells meeting, upper chest

cues: Dumbbells to upper chest level at bottom
Slight arc — press up and slightly back
Do not let shoulders roll forward at bottom
Control the negative — feel the stretch

why: Trains both directions of rotator cuff movement in a single exercise, offering a time-efficient way to cover shoulder joint health work that would otherwise need two separate exercises.

Use a light weight, this is a precision movement not a strength one
Move slowly and with control through both the internal and external phases

name: Dumbbell Kickback
description: Benched single-arm tricep extension moving behind torso
form_cues: Benched position, arm extended, full extension behind torso, full contraction
why: Heavy tricep exercise that allows significant loading through elbow extension. Develops the medial and lateral heads of the tricep.

name: Dumbbell Lateral Lunge

cues: Push the hips back as you step laterally
Keep the working knee tracking over the toes
Push off the working leg to return to centre

cues: Slight forward lean at hips for better leverage
Raise to shoulder height — no higher
Pinky slightly higher than thumb at top

Reset your breathing before the thruster portion

why: Trains the same shoulder stability and hip mobility as a barbell overhead squat with a lower technical barrier to entry.

Sit back into the hips as you descend
Keep the chest up and core braced

Drive the hips forward to stand tall

Keep elbows pinned at your sides

Curl to shoulder height without swinging

Push the knees out in line with the toes
Sit straight down rather than back

Keep dumbbells at shoulder height between reps
Finish each rep with full overhead lockout

Straighten the elbow, squeeze the triceps
Keep the upper arm still, only the forearm moves

Stop if sharp pain occurs, mild discomfort is expected

Progress load only once pain-free at bodyweight

Stop if sharp pain occurs at the elbow

Lower the crown of the head toward the floor
Press back to the starting pike position

Keep the core gently braced throughout

don't crane it up to look forward

Body in one straight line from head to heels
Elbows about 45 degrees from the body
Lower until the chest is near the floor
Push the floor away to straight arms

name: Thruster
description: A full body compound movement combining a squat and press. Targets legs, shoulders and core.
form_cues: Front rack, squat to depth, explosive drive, overhead lockout
why: Extremely high metabolic demand. Develops functional strength across multiple joints and is excellent for conditioning and fat loss.
cues: Squat down with bar at front rack or on shoulders
Drive up explosively using leg drive
Press overhead as you reach full extension

name: Tib Raises
description: Lean the back against a wall with the feet a short step out and the legs straight. Lift the toes up towards the shins, pause, then lower under control.
form_cues: Back against wall, feet 30cm out, heels planted, toes pulled high, slow lowering
why: Strengthens the tibialis anterior, the muscle at the front of the shin that lifts the foot. This supports ankle control and is commonly used to help manage shin soreness in runners.
cues: Keep the heels on the floor
Keep the legs straight and the back against the wall
Pull the toes up as far as possible

name: Tire Flip
description: Flipping a large tractor tire end over end, a full-body power and conditioning movement common in strongman training.
why: One of the highest-output full-body power movements available, training the deadlift-to-press pattern under real-world loading.
cues: Get low and drive with the legs on the initial lift, not the back
Push through as the tire reaches the tipping point
Reset your grip and stance between flips

name: Toe Yoga
description: Seated or standing drill isolating the big toe and other four toes, lifting the big toe while keeping the others down, then reversing.
why: Builds isolated motor control of the foot's intrinsic muscles, which supports arch stability and can help with plantar fasciitis and bunions.
cues: Move slowly, this is a control exercise not a strength one
Keep the rest of the foot relaxed while isolating the toes
Practice barefoot for the clearest feedback

name: Toes-to-Bar
description: Explosive hip flexion bringing toes to bar
form_cues: Dead hang, explosive hip drive, rhythm-based, power emphasis
why: Lower abs, power development, hip flexion power, grip
reps: Power: 5-10 reps, Conditioning: 10-25 reps, Volume: 15-30 reps
cues: Explosive hip drive bringing toes to bar.
Great power and lower ab builder.

name: Torso Rotation Machine
description: Seated machine that rotates the torso against resistance, isolating the obliques through a controlled rotational range.
why: Provides a stable, joint-friendly way to load rotational core strength without the technique demand of free-weight rotational work.
cues: Rotate from the torso, not by yanking with the arms

name: Towel Pull-Up
description: Pull-up gripping towel instead of bar
form_cues: Firm towel grip, full ROM, grip strength emphasis, controlled
why: Grip strength, forearm endurance, stability demand

name: Towel Scrunches
description: Sitting with a towel flat under the foot, scrunching the toes to pull the towel toward the heel, strengthening the intrinsic foot muscles.
why: One of the simplest and most accessible exercises for strengthening the intrinsic foot muscles, commonly used in plantar fasciitis rehab.
cues: Keep the heel in contact with the floor throughout
Use only the toes to scrunch the towel
Reset and repeat for the full set

name: Trap Bar Carry
description: Carrying trap bar at sides while walking
form_cues: Trap bar at sides, upright posture, core engaged, steady pace
why: Grip strength, core stability, carry variation

form_cues: Trap bar grip, explosive drive, full extension, control landing

name: Traveling Sit Thru
description: A ground-based movement from a hands and feet position. Lift one hand, kick the opposite leg under the body while rotating the chest up to the ceiling, then return and repeat while moving across the floor.
form_cues: Hands under shoulders, hips low, chest rotating open, controlled kick through, smooth alternating sides
why: Combines trunk rotation, shoulder support and hip mobility in one flowing movement, which builds coordination and body control. It also raises the heart rate a little as a floor-based warm-up or conditioning drill.
reps: 6-10 reps per side or 20-30 seconds, 2-3 rounds
cues: Keep the hips low and the core braced
Rotate the chest open as the leg threads through
Place the hands under the shoulders
Alternate sides and keep the steps even

name: Treadmill Running
description: Running on a treadmill at a controlled speed and incline for indoor aerobic training.
form_cues: Stay in the middle of the belt. Do not overstride to keep up with belt speed - let legs turn over naturally.
why: An effective exercise for developing strength, muscle size and movement quality in the targeted muscle groups.
cues: Set incline to 1-2% to simulate outdoors

name: Treadmill Sprints
description: High-speed sprint intervals on a treadmill. Set speed to near-max before jumping on.
form_cues: Set speed first, grab rails, feet on sides, release onto belt. Keep intervals short - 10-20 sec max at full speed.
why: High-intensity cardiovascular training that develops aerobic capacity, burns calories and improves conditioning with minimal time investment.
reps: Intervals: 10-20 sec at 16-22 km/h / Rest: 40-90 sec / Sets: 6-12
cues: Set treadmill to sprint speed before stepping on
Hold rails only to step on/off safely

name: Tricep Dips
description: Bodyweight or weighted dip emphasizing tricep
form_cues: Upright torso, elbows tucked, full ROM, explosive press, controlled descent
why: Bodyweight compound pressing movement that trains chest, triceps and front delts. The narrow hand position shifts emphasis to the triceps.
cues: Lower body with elbows tucked toward ribs

name: TRX Lat Stretch
description: Suspended in a TRX strap with arms extended, leaning back and away to stretch the lats through a loaded overhead position.
why: Stretches the lats through a fully overhead, loaded position, useful for improving overhead shoulder mobility limited by tight lat tissue.
reps: Hold 30-90 seconds per side | 2-3 sets | Breathe deeply and relax into the stretch
cues: Lean back gradually, controlling the stretch with your feet
Keep the ribs down rather than over-arching the low back
Hold and breathe rather than bouncing into the stretch

name: TRX Row
description: Horizontal pull on suspension trainer with angle adjustment
form_cues: Body angle for difficulty, full ROM, shoulder retraction
why: Progressive difficulty, core stability, posterior chain

name: Tuck Jumps
description: Vertical jump driving knees to chest at the peak. Builds explosive power and hip flexor strength.
form_cues: Explosive jump first, then tuck. Do not tuck early - it reduces height. Land quiet and springy.
why: Trains the lower abs and hip flexors through leg raise patterns. Develops the lower portion of the rectus abdominis often missed by crunches.
cues: Jump as high as possible before tucking knees
Pull knees to chest quickly at the top

name: Tuck Planche Hold
description: Static hold with knees tucked to the chest and body suspended forward on straight arms, an entry-level planche progression.
why: The foundational progression toward the full planche, building the forward-lean shoulder and core strength unique to this skill.
cues: Round the upper back, don't arch it
Push the floor away hard through straight arms
Keep the lean gradual, don't force it

name: Turkish Get-Up
description: Complex movement transitioning from lying to standing
form_cues: Kettlebell overhead, full ROM standing, eyes on weight, explosive
why: Full body coordination, shoulder stability, hip mobility, power
reps: Strength: 3-5 reps, Accessory: 5-10 reps, Volume: 8-15 reps
cues: Sit up and stand keeping overhead position.

name: Typewriter Pull-Up
description: Pull-up variation where the body is pulled to one side at the top and slid horizontally to the other side while staying elevated.
why: An advanced pulling variation that builds significant lat strength and control at end-range positions.
cues: Keep the chin above the bar throughout the horizontal slide
Move slowly and under control side to side
Keep the core tight to avoid swinging

name: V-Bar Tricep Pushdown
description: Cable tricep extension with V-bar attachment
form_cues: Standing upright, elbows at sides, full extension, constant tension
why: Isolates the triceps through a pushdown motion with constant cable tension. Effective for all three tricep heads with low joint stress.

why: A V-shaped guided leg press that tracks a slightly different angle than a standard leg press, allowing heavy quad and glute loading with a fixed, stable path and minimal spinal compression.

name: V-Up
description: Simultaneous upper and lower body flexion meeting
form_cues: Explosive simultaneous lift, touch toes, control descent, explosive
why: Full ab development, hip flexion, coordination
reps: Hypertrophy: 8-12 reps, Accessory: 10-15 reps, Volume: 12-20 reps
cues: Explosive simultaneous arm and leg lift.

why: One of the few cardio machines that meaningfully loads the upper body alongside the lower body, without the impact of running.

Use the whole range of motion available on the machine
Engage the core to stabilise the climbing motion

name: Vertical Leg Press
description: Vertical angle leg press variation for unique loading emphasis
form_cues: Vertical position, full ROM press, smooth tempo, consistent path
why: The vertical pressing angle changes the strength curve compared to a standard 45-degree leg press, allowing heavy quad and glute loading with a fixed, stable path and minimal spinal compression.

form_cues: Machine seated, full ROM, neutral spine, controlled tempo
why: Machine stability, controlled ROM, consistent training stimulus
cues: Machine path guides angle reducing stabilizer demand.
Perfect for deloads or volume training.

name: Walking
description: Brisk walking for low-impact aerobic conditioning. Often underrated as a fat-burning tool.
form_cues: Head up, chest open, arms swinging. Not a leisurely stroll - purposeful pace.
why: Low-impact cardiovascular exercise that builds aerobic base, burns calories and is joint-friendly for active recovery or general conditioning.
cues: Walk fast enough to elevate heart rate slightly

name: Walking Hip Openers
description: A dynamic warm-up drill done while walking forward. Lift one knee up and turn it out to the side, then step down and repeat on the other leg.
form_cues: Upright torso, knee lifted then rotated out, hips level, controlled step down
why: Takes the hip through lifting and outward rotation under light load, which warms up the hip joint before squatting, lunging or running. It also practises balance on one leg.
cues: Stand tall and keep the chest up
Lift the knee high before turning it out
Rotate from the hip, not the lower back
Step down with control and stay balanced
Alternate legs in a smooth rhythm

name: Walking Lunge
description: A walking lunge covering ground with alternating forward steps.
form_cues: Step forward, 90° angles, alternating legs, upright torso
why: Develops single-leg strength, balance and coordination simultaneously. Higher metabolic demand than stationary lunges.
reps: Hypertrophy: 10-16 steps per leg | Conditioning: 20+ steps per leg | 3-4 sets
cues: Step forward into a lunge — long stride
Front shin vertical — knee does not cave
Rear knee almost touches the floor
Drive through front heel to step forward

Focus on the shoulder blades rotating, not just the arms moving

why: Builds the shoulder strength, core control, and confidence needed as a stepping stone toward freestanding handstands.

Keep the core braced to avoid over-arching

form_cues: Seated/lying, weight at chest, curl up, full contraction, light weight start
why: Trains the rectus abdominis through spinal flexion. Classic ab exercise that builds core endurance and definition.

description: A hang from a pull-up bar with arms straight and extra weight added, usually on a dip belt. It is a loaded version of the dead hang.
form_cues: Full overhand grip, straight arms, shoulders packed down, ribs tight, no swinging, weight centred under the hips, step down before grip fails
why: Builds grip and forearm strength and shoulder and lat endurance by holding bodyweight plus extra load. It suits people who can already hang for around a minute.
reps: 20-40 second holds, 3-5 sets with about 10 percent of bodyweight added
cues: Grip the bar fully, thumbs around it
Hang with arms straight, shoulders gently pulled down
Keep the weight still, no swinging
Squeeze the ribs down and keep the body tight
Step down safely when the grip fails

Control the plate rather than using momentum to swing it

Drive elbows down and out to your sides
Lead with the chest towards the bar
Lower under control to straight arms
